display_name: Yashovarman of Kannauj & Lalitaditya of Kashmir
one_line: Rival north-Indian kings locked in a high-stakes struggle for prestige between Kannauj and Kashmir in the mid-8th century.

appearance.age_look: Late 20s for Yashovarman, early 30s for Lalitaditya; both athletic, upright and battle-trained.
appearance.face: Yashovarman has an oval face, warm medium-brown complexion, sharp nose, thin moustache and focused, slightly idealistic eyes with a calm, determined expression; Lalitaditya has a broader jaw, slightly lighter brown complexion, thicker arched brows, fuller moustache with a short neatly trimmed beard and an intense, assessing gaze, often wearing a faint, confident half-smile.
appearance.hair: Yashovarman’s straight black hair is shoulder-length, center-parted, gathered back into a low cloth-wrapped knot at the nape; Lalitaditya’s wavy black hair is slightly longer, tied into a high warrior topknot with a narrow cloth band, a few controlled strands framing his temples; neither wears a metal crown, only practical cloth headbands suited for travel and campaign.
appearance.costume: Yashovarman wears a mid-8th-century north Indian royal warrior outfit from the upper Ganga plains: a long-sleeved, knee-length, side-tied cotton angarkha in rich deep red with subtle gold border bands, belted at the waist with a broad dark brown leather girdle; over this a sleeveless quilted textile coat in muted dull gold with simple diamond stitching for light protection, and a soft off-white cotton dhoti wrapped to mid-calf with neat pleats in front; his feet are in brown leather strapped sandals; his jewellery is restrained—two thin gold armlets on each upper arm, a single simple gold torque necklace, and small round gold ear-studs; he occasionally wears a plain off-white cotton shawl with a thin red edge draped over one shoulder for court scenes; Lalitaditya’s costume reflects a Kashmiri royal commander: a long, slightly flared, calf-length woolen tunic (phiran-like) in deep indigo with a narrow V-neck and woven geometric bands in muted saffron and cream at cuffs and hem, belted with a dark indigo cloth sash over which sits a practical brown leather belt; underneath is a lighter undyed wool under-tunic peeking at the neck; his lower garment is a close-wrapped off-white churidar-style trouser tucked into soft mid-calf brown leather boots suitable for highland marches; over his tunic he wears a fitted quilted vest in dark teal with horizontal stitch lines, giving subtle armour without fantasy plates; his ornaments are modest but royal—one engraved copper-gold armlet on the right arm, a simple signet ring, and small teardrop gold earrings; in colder scenes he can have a heavy woolen shawl in muted saffron, but the default is without it.
appearance.signature: Yashovarman’s signature weapon is a long, slightly curved single-edged sword with a plain steel blade, a simple crossguard and a brown leather-wrapped hilt worn at his left hip; Lalitaditya’s signature weapon is a sturdy straight-bladed steel sword with a slightly broader blade and a round pommel, slung from his belt on his left side, both swords kept unornamented to stress function over display.

ref_desc: Yashovarman is a medium-brown, oval-faced warrior-king with shoulder-length black hair in a low knot, deep red angarkha, quilted dull-gold vest, off-white dhoti, leather sandals and a plain curved sword, while Lalitaditya is a slightly lighter brown, broad-jawed king with wavy black hair in a high topknot, deep indigo wool tunic with saffron-cream borders, dark teal quilted vest, off-white close trousers, leather boots and a straight steel sword; both share a restrained gold-and-brown palette.
sheet_prompt: Draw two full-body anime-style model figures, Yashovarman and Lalitaditya, standing side by side against a neutral background for consistent character reference: Yashovarman is a medium-brown, oval-faced north Indian king in his late 20s with a sharp nose, thin moustache and focused eyes, straight black hair to the shoulders gathered into a low cloth-wrapped knot, wearing a long-sleeved knee-length deep red cotton angarkha with subtle gold borders, belted by a broad dark brown leather girdle, over which sits a sleeveless dull-gold quilted textile vest, an off-white dhoti wrapped to mid-calf with neat pleats, and brown leather strapped sandals; his ornaments are two thin gold armlets on each upper arm, a single simple gold torque, and small round gold ear-studs, and at his left hip hangs his signature weapon, a plain long slightly curved steel sword with a simple crossguard and brown leather-wrapped hilt; beside him, Lalitaditya is a slightly lighter brown, broad-jawed Kashmiri king in his early 30s with thicker brows, a fuller moustache and short neat beard, wavy black hair tied into a high warrior topknot with a narrow cloth band and a few strands at the temples, wearing a calf-length deep indigo woolen tunic with a narrow V-neck and woven saffron and cream geometric borders at cuffs and hem, cinched by a dark indigo cloth sash and a brown leather belt, over a dark teal fitted quilted vest, with off-white close-fitting trousers tucked into mid-calf brown leather boots; his jewellery is a single engraved copper-gold armlet, a signet ring and small teardrop gold earrings, and his left side carries a straight-bladed steel sword with a round pommel; keep both fully clothed and modest, colours anchored in deep red, indigo, muted gold, off-white and brown leather, with dignified heroic postures and clear front-facing views to show face, hair, clothing details and weapons consistently.
